claims.text: High configurational entropy creates a disordered lattice in high-entropy alloys.
The disordered lattice in high-entropy alloys hinders dislocation motion.
Lattice disorder promotes alternative deformation mechanisms such as twinning.
Atomic-scale lattice distortions produce a disordered microstructure that impedes dislocation motion.
Elevated configurational entropy raises the activation barriers for dislocation motion.
Under dynamic loading, impeded dislocation motion forces activation of secondary deformation modes such as twinning.
Activation of secondary deformation modes contributes to enhanced strength.
Activation of secondary deformation modes helps maintain ductility.
Under dynamic loading, the high-entropy alloy will exhibit higher strength than the conventional low-entropy alloy.
Under dynamic loading, the high-entropy alloy will exhibit ductility comparable to or greater than that of the conventional low-entropy alloy.
The proposed mechanism applies to single-phase high-entropy alloys with similar microstructural features and compositions at room temperature from quasi-static through high dynamic strain rates.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome permits ductility merely comparable to the baseline, whereas the falsification rule requires a statistically significant improvement in both strength and ductility. Thus, an observation of higher strength with unchanged ductility could agree with the prediction yet trigger the stated falsification rule.
